changes.finding: C02 buffering, frame decode and version comparison attribution
changes.reason: Gen::read owns accumulation and I/O framing boundaries; decode checks the frame and extracts Ready.version; Gen::route performs the VERSION compatibility comparison.

before: Decoder accumulates partial frames and rejects EOF mid-frame, malformed messages and unaccounted descriptors.
Ready must be first with the exact protocol version; replies must match request kind and tree ID; reused tree IDs and duplicate exits end the generation.
Waiters are removed only after validation; life notifications and reply delivery occur outside the lock. Earliest missed asynchronous deadline kills the generation.
after: Gen::read buffers partial frames, rejects EOF mid-frame and unaccounted descriptors, and propagates malformed-frame errors from omni-proto::decode.
Gen::route requires Ready first and compares its version with VERSION. Replies must match request kind and tree ID; reused tree IDs and duplicate exits end the generation.
Waiters are removed only after validation; life notifications and reply delivery occur outside the lock. Earliest missed asynchronous deadline kills the generation.

before: client/channel.rs owns pending requests, trees and death propagation.
after: omni-proto::decode validates framing and extracts message fields, including the transmitted Ready version; omni-proto::VERSION supplies the expected version for the separate comparison in Gen::route.
client/channel.rs owns pending requests, trees and death propagation.

changes.finding: C02 ordinary identity kill path versus failed-handoff fallback and macOS identity cases
changes.reason: The ordinary Watch/Ident path and Keeper::adopt fallback are distinct. The macOS match distinguishes absent captured identity from captured identity whose current lookup is absent or different, after the exit checks.

before: Creates a reaper thread before process creation, then adopts the Child and records an identity before handoff.
Linux opens a pidfd, verifies a live child in /proc and signal-0 liveness, and sends SIGKILL only through that descriptor.
macOS precreates a kqueue, tracks NOTE_EXIT and records start time; kill checks the watch and start time immediately before signaling.
after: Creates a reaper thread before process creation, then adopts the Child and records an identity before handoff.
On Linux, Ident::adopt opens a pidfd and retains it after live-child /proc and signal-0 checks; the ordinary Watch::kill to Ident::kill path sends SIGKILL through that descriptor.
macOS precreates a kqueue, tracks NOTE_EXIT and records start time; the ordinary Ident::kill path checks the watch and start time immediately before signaling.
Separately, Keeper::adopt handles a failed Child handoff to the reaper by calling Child::kill and Child::wait, ignoring both results, before returning the Watch.

before: Unknown identity means Abandoned; no unverified numeric PID is intentionally signaled.
after: In the ordinary Watch/Ident kill path, a missing Linux pidfd returns Abandoned. On macOS, a recorded or newly observed exit returns Gone first; otherwise, an absent captured start time returns Abandoned, while a captured start with a missing or different current start time is classified Gone.

before: macOS retains a documented check-to-signal PID-reuse window. Missing Linux pidfd or macOS identity leaves a stuck process running.
after: The ordinary macOS Ident::kill path retains a documented check-to-signal PID-reuse window despite its identity checks.

The pidfd-only and identity-based abandonment statements are scoped to the ordinary Watch/Ident path. Keeper::adopt has the separate failed-handoff Child::kill/wait fallback; this file does not establish the standard-library internals of those operations.

changes.finding: C02 empty process inventory is not exclusive to the local gone fast path
changes.reason: life.gone gives an immediate empty vector, but the non-lost request path returns Answer::Processes(list) unchanged and has no nonempty-list requirement.

before: Lazily creates a dedicated multithread Tokio runtime with I/O and time, independent of the caller runtime and checked against creator PID.
spawn uses a shared registry with a 10 s request deadline and 20 s join bound; Unix PTY roots stay held until reader setup and Go.
Tree caches exit via watch state; stop uses cleanup admission and awaits Stopped, resize is fire-and-forget, and process inventory returns empty only once gone.
after: Lazily creates a dedicated multithread Tokio runtime with I/O and time, independent of the caller runtime and checked against creator PID.
spawn uses a shared registry with a 10 s request deadline and 20 s join bound; Unix PTY roots stay held until reader setup and Go.

Tree caches exit via watch state; stop uses cleanup admission and awaits Stopped, and resize is fire-and-forget. processes returns an empty vector immediately when life.gone is set; otherwise, after the loss check, it returns the supervisor's Processes list unchanged, including an empty list.

changes.finding: C02 configure cutoff uses first startup attempt, including failure
changes.reason: The caller passes CURRENT.started(); num is incremented before open and is not rolled back on its failure. configure_in checks same-path idempotence before rejecting a true started flag.

before: Changing configured path after startup is refused, but setting the same path is idempotent.
Unix module candidate and binary must be owned by user/root and not group/other writable.
after: The configure cutoff is Registry::started() (num > 0): get increments num before its first open attempt and retains it after a failed attempt; configure_in refuses a different path when that flag is true but accepts the same configured path idempotently.
Unix module candidate and binary must be owned by user/root and not group/other writable.
